article.title: Bangladesh Faces Mounting Climate Crisis While Wealthy, Polluting Nations Resist Calls to Pay Up
article.content: Bangladesh’s first riverkeeper, Sharif Jamil, shares how poor countries in the Global South are struggling to effectively adapt to climate change as rising sea levels, extreme weather patterns, pollution and more are creating an escalating “humanitarian catastrophe,” while the wealthy impede efforts to reallocate financial resources for adaptation and mitigation. “If you want to protect the planet, if you want to save the planet from global warming, you need climate finance to make all this transition,” says Jamil.
